title: Start with the decision, not the visual
subject: visualization
basis: Metadata/title rule; organizational placement, not scientific validation

Specify the audience, decision, observation grain, metric definition, comparison and action before selecting a renderer. The Shortlist has three active experiments and three reserves; this is the owner’s portfolio limit, not a universal Power BI rule. Its acceptance rule asks about decision value, a simpler alternative, reusability and ownership cost. A pattern can fail this rule despite looking impressive. Keep the proposed business benefit separate from an observed outcome; none of the three active Shortlist ideas is recorded as implemented.

title: Distribution Detective: build and challenge the bins
subject: visualization
basis: Metadata/title rule; organizational placement, not scientific validation
context: REVIEW ONLY — The same mean can describe different service processes. A histogram groups individual observations into numeric intervals; the interval boundaries are part of the analysis. The linked W39 challenge uses clinic waiting-time practice data, not independently authenticated clinical observations. Its source requests disconnected width and bin-axis tables and a count measure so the reader can vary width. Built-in Power BI binning is a separate, fixed-field grouping feature: adding a slicer does not automatically make that field’s bin size dynamic. Use half-open intervals [start, start + width) so a boundary observation belongs to exactly one bin. For unequal widths, frequency height is misleading: density must preserve area meaning.

title: Smart Filter Console: field names are not field values

A console must distinguish choosing the analytical dimension from choosing members of that dimension. Test reset, multiple selection, hierarchy persistence and empty-result states. title: Metric Navigator: reconcile identities before explaining causes
subject: visualization
basis: Broad subject placement; finer editorial mapping pending
context: REVIEW ONLY — A metric map is a calculation graph whose branches explain how totals are built. A signed additive identity reconciles a parent change to signed child changes. For a product A×B, the W40 source gives a midpoint split: ΔA times the average of B’s two-period values, and ΔB times the average of A’s values. The contributions sum algebraically to the product change. This is an accounting decomposition, not evidence that a component caused a business outcome. Share a measure definition across repeated branches while forbidding cycles along an ancestor path. A generic decomposition tree is a useful native comparison baseline, but its dimension splits are not automatically a renderer of arbitrary formula operators.

title: Compact SVG indicators: preserve the uncapped number
subject: visualization
basis: Broad subject placement; finer editorial mapping pending
context: REVIEW ONLY — An SVG ring encodes progress in a compact cell; a numeric label carries the actual ratio. The W38 challenge shows inline SVG generated by DAX inside a standard table, under a no-AppSource constraint. This does not mean SVG is always the easiest or fastest choice. Compare a native data bar or a clear actual/target column first. Keep raw progress separate from a visually clamped arc: exceeding a target should remain visible in the number even if a circle cannot show more than one turn. Zero or absent targets need a deliberate unavailable state. The source includes typographic quotation marks in illustrative markup; that text must not be copied blindly as executable XML/DAX.

title: Bump charts: explain rank movement and its population
subject: visualization
basis: Broad subject placement; finer editorial mapping pending
context: REVIEW ONLY — A bump chart places rank on the quantitative axis and time on the ordered axis, with one series per entity. The W33 page describes a native line-chart approach but its field-well sentence places Program Name on Y and Rank in Legend; that wording conflicts with the intended rank chart. Preserve the source sentence in raw extraction and record the correction as a reviewer proposal. A defensible implementation instead tests time on X, numeric rank on Y, and program/entity as series, with rank 1 at the top.

title: Ternary cross-sell: three shares, one customer
subject: visualization
basis: Broad subject placement; finer editorial mapping pending

The center means a balanced mix, not high revenue or good profit. A small specialist may be near the same vertex as a large specialist; include magnitude and exact values separately. Category shares with a zero or negative total, missing categories or returns require a defined policy before geometry. Source classification rules overlap at 60/20/20: both specialist and balanced conditions are met. A deterministic implementation must explicitly resolve the overlap rather than quietly pretending the source defines precedence.

title: Measures respond to context; stored columns serve a different job
subject: visualization
basis: Broad subject placement; finer editorial mapping pending
context: REVIEW ONLY — A measure is evaluated in the query’s filter context. A stored calculated column expresses row-level values at model-processing time and can support grouping or sorting. Neither choice is universally superior. A reusable report metric must specify the active relationships and filter behavior; adding a slicer cannot repair a disconnected dimension. CALCULATE changes evaluation context according to its filters, so a correct-looking total still needs context tests. Preserve a numeric metric when formatting it: string conversion can undermine numeric sorting, axes and later arithmetic. Dynamic format strings are a relevant alternative when a measure needs different numeric presentation.

title: Grain and denominators: the hidden structure of a chart
subject: visualization
basis: Metadata/title rule; organizational placement, not scientific validation
context: REVIEW ONLY — A chart encodes the measure supplied to it, including any grain error. Multi-line orders are not multiple distinct orders; customers are not rows. Ratios should be derived from coherent totals and denominators in the same context. An average of subgroup averages can disagree with the overall rate when groups have different sizes. In the linked financial exercise, order identity is a composite of Order ID, Order Date, Customer ID and Location ID. Preserve that scenario-specific rule; it is not a universal definition of an order key. Missing, zero and negative denominators have different interpretations and must not be flattened into a fabricated zero.

title: Design interaction that does not depend on hover or color

basis: Metadata/title rule; organizational placement, not scientific validation

Provide meaningful titles, alt text, logical tab order and non-color labels. Remove purely decorative objects from keyboard navigation while keeping functional controls reachable. Dynamic descriptions should reflect the active context; a fixed description can become inaccurate after filtering. Automated structure checks do not replace actual keyboard, screen-reader, high-contrast and touch testing.

title: Measure the bottleneck before changing the renderer
subject: visualization
basis: Broad subject placement; finer editorial mapping pending
context: REVIEW ONLY — Performance is a measured property of a workload, not a visual brand. Performance Analyzer provides visual-level timing categories, while DAX Studio server timings can investigate model-query behavior in an appropriate environment. Rendering fewer primitives may help one bottleneck and do nothing for an expensive measure. Keep dataset, filter context, device, connection mode and cache conditions comparable. title: Native, Deneb or HTML: choose the smallest adequate capability
subject: visualization
basis: Metadata/title rule; organizational placement, not scientific validation
context: REVIEW ONLY — Use native visuals as a baseline, Deneb when a grammar of graphics adds analytical capability, and HTML Content for justified rich composition under its constraints. HTML in a Power BI custom visual is not a general browser application: sandboxing, edition, host and permissions affect behavior. The regular and secure editions have different allowed content and export characteristics. A certified visual is not automatically accessible or suitable for every workload. The authoring choice must preserve selection identity, filter interaction, readability and maintainability.

title: Scale choices change the argument
subject: visualization
basis: Broad subject placement; finer editorial mapping pending
context: REVIEW ONLY — When bar length encodes a value, the baseline affects perceived ratios; cutting it can manufacture an exaggerated contrast. A line chart primarily encodes position and changes along an ordered sequence, so an appropriate range can differ, but it must still be disclosed and interpreted honestly. Logarithmic axes represent multiplicative ratios, not equal additive differences, and standard log axes cannot represent zero or negative values. Dual axes can create apparent relationships through scale selection. Choose comparable small multiples or indexed series when their interpretation better matches the question.

title: Small multiples: keep comparison conditions visible
subject: visualization
basis: Metadata/title rule; organizational placement, not scientific validation
context: REVIEW ONLY — Faceting repeats a consistent view for groups, reducing overplotting and making local patterns easier to inspect. Comparability depends on units, axes, observation range and definitions. A panel with an independently scaled axis can be useful for shape, but it cannot support casual absolute-height comparison with a differently scaled panel. Small multiples also consume space; many tiny panels can be less readable than a targeted filter or summary table. The W39 pattern uses site panels specifically to contrast distributions under shared bin choices.

title: Distinguish description, association and causal evidence
subject: visualization
basis: Broad subject placement; finer editorial mapping pending
context: REVIEW ONLY — A display can be accurate about the sample and still support an invalid inference. Check population, sampling, missingness and aggregation before generalizing. Association can change after stratification; aggregation can hide different group sizes and opposing subgroup patterns. A confidence interval expresses uncertainty under a statistical procedure and assumptions, not a guarantee about future individual cases. Statistical significance does not establish practical importance, and a p-value is not the probability that the null is true. Keep these interpretations distinct when generating explanatory cards or executive narratives.

title: Choose an argument shape after the evidence survives
subject: visualization
basis: Metadata/title rule; organizational placement, not scientific validation

The collection distinguishes a compressed Big Idea, an executive answer-first structure, contrast for a change proposal, and an analytical What/So what/Now what handoff. Keep source-specific attributions attached to the source rather than treating every framework label as an independently verified universal rule. A causal spine is dangerous if its “because” clauses exceed the study design. If no decision owner or meaningful action exists, an annotated chart may be a better deliverable than a dramatic story.

title: Turn an insight into an inspectable decision chain

basis: Metadata/title rule; organizational placement, not scientific validation
